About Chainlink Labs

Chainlink Labs is one of the primary contributing developers of Chainlink, the standard for onchain finance enabling high-quality data, secure cross-chain interoperability, and compliant connectivity across global markets. Chainlink powers leading tokenized assets, financial institutions, market infrastructures, and decentralized applications by providing secure access to real-world data, cross-chain messaging, and blockchain connectivity across any network. The Chainlink standard has enabled tens of trillions of dollars in transaction value and is helping unify global markets onchain. Many of the world’s largest financial services institutions have also adopted Chainlink’s standards and infrastructure, including Swift, Euroclear, Mastercard, Fidelity International, UBS, S&P Dow Jones Indices, FTSE Russell, WisdomTree, ANZ, Aave, Polymarket, Lido, and many others.

Chainlink Labs is a world-class team of developers, researchers, and capital markets experts, and has ranked among Fortune's Best Workplaces in Technology, Fortune's Best Medium Workplace, and the Top 100 Global Most Loved Workplaces. Learn more at chain.link or chainlinklabs.com.

About The Role

Join Chainlink Labs, a leading decentralized oracle network company, as a high-impact Executive Assistant and strategic thought partner to our senior leadership. In this dynamic role, you’ll go beyond traditional support—serving as the right hand to our executives and playing a key role in driving operational excellence. From managing complex calendars and high-stakes meetings to navigating sensitive information with discretion, you’ll be trusted to anticipate needs, streamline workflows, and help power our fast-paced, high-performance journey. If you’re proactive, sharp, and thrive in an environment where every day is different, we want to meet you. We don't have an assigned team for this role and will put people where they will best shine!

For this role, we are looking for someone in NYC. This role will be in office full time to provide additional executive support.

Your Impact

  • Act as a gatekeeper for the executive’s time and focus - managing and prioritizing requests from across the business and the external ecosystem.

  • Successfully coordinate and execute department meetings and communications, ensuring smooth collaboration and efficient information flow.

  • Demonstrate the highest level of discretion when handling sensitive information, recognizing the importance of safeguarding the interests of Chainlink Labs.

  • Exhibit excellent written communication skills, as you will be communicating largely in text and taking important notes for various engagements.

  • Be a right-hand person to the executive team, partnering with them to help efficiently navigate their private and professional lives.

  • Own and deliver on a wide variety of projects and initiatives for the executive team.

Requirements

  • Experience delivering a high touch support model, anticipating needs, and establishing seamless processes across core executive support tasks, e.g. scheduling, travel, communications, records, and reports.

  • Experience as an Executive Assistant managing sensitive data and commitment to maintaining confidentiality within a security-focused company environment.

  • Experience in a multi-time-zone/global setting

  • Willingness to work outside usual business hours with a high sense of urgency.

  • Strong self-management, time management, and organizational skills to effectively handle multiple tasks.

  • Excellent written communication level, capable of articulating ideas and communicating clearly in writing.

  • Experience using tact, sound business judgment, a solid understanding of our business, and impeccable time management, managing and prioritizing the C-Suite’s schedule and business obligations.

Preferred Requirements

  • Experience in small-medium tech startup environments, accustomed to working in agile and ownership-driven settings.

  • Event planning experience, demonstrating the ability to organize successful team offsites for the executive’s department.

  • Experience working on a team of highly collaborative EA’s, sharing insights, representing the executives effectively, and contributing positively to our company culture.

Chainlink Labs is a remote-first organization and employment eligibility is contingent upon residing in an approved hiring jurisdiction. Team members may work outside their primary country of legal residence for a maximum of 90 days per calendar year. Please discuss your current location, legal residence, and work authorization with your recruiter during your initial conversation. Unless otherwise stated for a specific role, we require working hours that overlap with Eastern Time (ET).

We carefully review all applications and aim to provide a response to every candidate within two weeks after the job posting closes. The closing date is listed on the job advert, so we encourage you to take the time to thoughtfully prepare your application. We want to fully consider your experience and skills, and you will hear from us regarding the status of your application shortly after the closing date.

Commitment to Equal Opportunity

Chainlink Labs is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment in compliance with applicable laws, regulations, or ordinances. If you need assistance or accommodation due to a disability or special need when applying for a role or in our recruitment process, please contact us via this form.

Global Data Privacy Notice for Job Candidates and Applicants

Information collected and processed as part of your Chainlink Labs Careers profile, and any job applications you choose to submit, is subject to our Recruiting Privacy Policy. By submitting your application, you are agreeing to our use and processing of your data as required.

Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.
OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves.
Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er. OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.

About the Opportunity

Enterprise Efficiency builds internal products and platforms that power how our company operates globally.
We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to own and improve our Payroll, Global Compensation, and Leave and Absence systems. You should bring deep, hands-on expertise in at least one of these domains, along with a working understanding of the core processes, system capabilities, and interdependencies across the other two.
You will partner closely with People, Payroll, Total Rewards, Finance, and Engineering to translate complex policies and operational requirements into reliable, intuitive, and scalable products. This is a hands-on product role, with ownership from problem discovery and process design through delivery, adoption, and continuous improvement.
Professional working proficiency in both English and Mandarin is required for product documentation, meetings, and cross-functional collaboration.
 
 

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Turn HR domain expertise into effective products. Understand the policies, operational processes, and user needs across Payroll, Global Compensation, and Leave and Absence. Work with domain specialists to translate these into clear product capabilities that simplify work for employees, managers, and operational teams.
  • Own the product roadmap for your scope. Partner with People, Payroll, Total Rewards, and Finance stakeholders to prioritize system foundations and efficiency opportunities.
  • Redesign end-to-end workflows. Improve processes such as payroll input validation and reconciliation, compensation reviews and changes, and leave requests and balance management. Define clear business rules, effective dates, approvals, exceptions, and ownership, with support from the relevant domain experts.
  • Connect HR systems and strengthen data integrity. Partner with engineering to integrate HRIS, payroll providers, compensation tools, and leave systems, improve data consistency, and deliver connected user experiences with appropriate permissions and audit trails.
  • Improve efficiency through automation and AI. Work with internal stakeholders to identify and implement practical solutions that reduce repetitive work and improve accuracy and decision quality.
  • Lead delivery, adoption, and business outcomes. Align engineering, design, and functional owners from discovery through rollout and continuous improvement. Measure results through cycle time, manual effort, accuracy, adoption, and control effectiveness.
 

What We Look For In You

    • 5+ years of experience in product management or closely related enterprise product roles, with substantial experience delivering HR or People systems.
    • A track record of independently owning enterprise products or major product initiatives from discovery through launch and adoption, with measurable improvements in operational efficiency, accuracy, or user experience.
    • Deep, hands-on expertise in at least one of the following domains: Payroll, Global Compensation, or Leave and Absence, including its business processes, policy rules, data dependencies, and operational exceptions. A working understanding of the core processes and system capabilities in the other two domains, including how all three connect, is required.
    • Demonstrated ability to translate complex HR policies and operational processes into clear product requirements, workflows, data models, and acceptance criteria.
    • Strong product judgment, with experience defining roadmaps, resolving competing priorities, and evaluating build-versus-buy options in partnership with business and engineering teams.
    • Technical fluency in enterprise integrations, data dependencies, identity, permissions, and auditability.
    • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, including the ability to challenge assumptions, explain tradeoffs, and build alignment across teams.
    • Ability to work effectively in both English and Mandarin, including writing product documents, participating in meetings, and collaborating across teams.
 

Nice to Haves

    • Experience with Workday, Oracle HCM, SAP SuccessFactors, UKG/Kronos, or equivalent HR systems and payroll platforms.
    • Experience delivering cross-border or multi-country projects, including coordinating teams across regions and managing local requirements.
    • Experience deploying AI or agent capabilities into production workflows and measuring their business impact.
    • Experience in financial services, crypto, payments, or another environment with demanding control and audit requirements.
    • Experience consolidating fragmented HR tools and improving data quality and ownership across systems.
 

Perks & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package
  • L&D programs and Education subsidy for employees' growth and development
  • Various team building programs and company events
  • Wellness and meal allowances 
  • Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependants

About Riot Platforms

Riot’s (NASDAQ: RIOT) vision is to be the world’s most trusted platform for powering and building digital infrastructure. Riot’s mission is to empower the future of digital infrastructure by positively impacting the sectors, networks, and communities that we touch. We believe that the combination of an innovative spirit and strong community partnership allows us to achieve best-in-class execution and create successful outcomes.

Who we are

At Riot, we’re building the future of digital infrastructure. Our team members have unparalleled opportunities to work on groundbreaking initiatives. Through technical excellence and strategic execution, Riot has positioned itself as a leader in the industry driving advancements that continue to set new benchmarks in digital infrastructure. 

We are trailblazers. Problem solvers. People who thrive in fast paced environments, communicate clearly, and bring relentless focus to efficiency and execution.

About the role

As a Mining Operations Supervisor, you will lead by example and oversee daily building operations, spending most of your time in the field supporting your teams. You will monitor critical systems, assign work to the appropriate crews, and coordinate with other supervisors and departments. You will also take ownership of the miner deployment, promote safety, and keep thorough records of maintenance and activity. This role includes overnight shifts, on-call rotations, and periodic assignments to new buildings, projects, and teams.

What you'll do

  • Manage a team of assistant supervisors and technicians.
  • Spend about 80% of your time in the field supporting teams and 20% in the office on computer-based tasks.
  • Promote and implement safety policies.
  • Take ownership of the miner deployment and see it through to successful completion.
  • Monitor pressure levels, tank temperatures, and tripped switch gears (breakers) using the Block ops site.
  • Assign building work tasks to the appropriate crews and attend shift pass down.
  • Conduct building walkthroughs to identify issues and safety hazards, and report findings to the appropriate teams.
  • Track maintenance updates, communications, and concerns in the Teams channel, Block ops, and OneNote, and respond as needed.
  • Record daily and weekly activities and reports in OneNote and the Teams channel.
  • Monitor Grafana for drops in miner performance.
  • Coordinate with other supervisors to distribute crews evenly across the site.
  • Monitor the on-call list and collaborate with teams to resolve issues promptly.

As Needed

  • Work overnight shifts and rotate on the on-call list weekly, as assigned.
  • Rotate to new buildings, projects, and miner transfer work orders quarterly, and to new teams annually.
  • Submit a monthly report on your assigned building.
  • Update the department on-call list, approve time sheets, and verify that team timecards are reviewed.
  • Check network switches, and ensure dry cooler winterization protocols are followed.
  • Coordinate with miner maintenance to optimize hash rate, and maintain parts and materials inventory, reporting status to the manager.
  • Coordinate contractors, electrical maintenance, and temporary material storage with inventory.
  • Cover for absent supervisors (team, building, or project), report issues to them, and act as acting assistant supervisor.
  • Have your team support other departments.
  • Ensure buildings are clean and presentable for tours.
  • Monitor buildings during 4CP shutdowns.
  • Participate in interview committees, and develop new procedures and S.O.P.s.
  • Attend all meetings and arrive on time.
  • Perform other related responsibilities as assigned to support operational needs and team success.

What you'll bring

  • High School Diploma or GED 
  • Excellent communication and multitasking skills 
  • Excellent problem-solving skills 
  • Detail-oriented and highly organized

Compensation and Benefits 

  • Competitive Salary: Base range (commensurate with experience) + bonus + sign-on equity grant. 
  • Long-Term Growth: Eligible to participate in Riot’s equity incentive programs and share in the success you help build. 
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan: Incudes a generous company match. 
  • Comprehensive Health Coverage: Multiple medical plan options, including 100% company-paid plans. 
  • Wellness & Lifestyle Perks: Enjoy free gym memberships, pet insurance, childcare discounts, and more to support your life both in and out of work. 

Riot is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Most iGaming brands sound exactly the same. We're hiring someone to make sure Dicey never does.

You'll be the voice of Dicey on social every day, X first. You come up with the ideas, make most of the content yourself, and own the voice, output and growth of our main accounts. You'll report to our Marketing Lead, who sets the strategy, and you'll get full autonomy on how we show up.

Think of the coolest person at the party. Everyone wants to talk to them, they always have the line, and they never lose their composure when things get messy. That's the account we want.

Basically, an organised degen.

What you'll actually do

  • Run Dicey's main accounts day to day, with X as the priority: posting, replying, trend-jacking and community.

  • Come up with ideas. Lots of them. Turn launches, wins and world events into moments people share.

  • Make most of the content yourself: posts, memes, graphics and short-form video. Our creative team backs you up on bigger video production.

  • React in real time. When the internet moves, we're in it while it's still relevant.

  • Walk the line: edgy enough to be remembered, never at the expense of the brand. Know when to bite and when to let the FUD die on its own.

  • Build and run KOL partnerships that amplify what we're pushing through our main accounts.

  • Work with product on launches and announcements.

  • Track what's working and turn results into clear, simple reporting.

You'll fit if

  • You're online too much and you know it. You live in internet culture, and you know iGaming Twitter and crypto Twitter are different crowds.

  • You write posts that are genuinely funny, sharp and on-trend, and you write them fast.

  • You make your own content. You don't need a designer or an editor to ship a meme, a graphic or a short video.

  • You know the difference between edgy and cringe, and between bold and brand-damaging.

  • Drama doesn't scare you. When Dicey gets pulled in, you handle it with precision and make sure we come out on top.

  • You've worked with KOLs or creators and know how to run a partnership that actually moves numbers.

  • You're comfortable with the numbers: reach, engagement, traffic, and what to do about them.

  • You're proactive. You don't need permission to have an idea, and you don't need chasing to deliver it.

  • You're comfortable working in online casino and sports betting.

Nice to have

  • You're iGaming native.

  • You can show us posts or campaigns of yours that took off.

  • You can name the last brand that made you laugh on X.

What you get

  • Full ownership of the voice of a brand that's growing fast.

  • Room to grow as the team grows.

  • Competitive compensation.

  • Remote, global team.

The small print

  • If it goes viral, it was your idea.

  • If it flops, it was also your idea. Post the next one anyway.

The Monad Foundation is a team of dedicated ecosystem and community builders who are on a mission to massively grow the impact of decentralized tech. We believe that the Monad blockchain--the performant and parallel EVM Layer 1--will help decentralized apps eat the world.

The Role

The Monad network was built for high frequency: 10,000 TPS, sub-second finality, full EVM compatibility. Trading is the use case that tests that claim hardest, and you’ll be the person who brings the best trading teams to build on it.

You’ll sit in the room when a perps team, a DEX, or a trading terminal decides which chain to deploy on. You’ll own the relationship from first call through launch and beyond, and you’ll be a public voice for trading on the Monad network on podcasts, panels, and in long-form content.

This is a senior individual contributor role with end to end ownership. You’ll work across ecosystem, defi, marketing, and events at Monad Foundation, and alongside core contributors on technical onboarding. Monad Foundation is a core contributor to the Monad protocol, and this role supports builders on the network as one of many ecosystem participants.

What You’ll Do

  • Bring leading trading applications to the Monad network: perps and spot DEXs, aggregators, trading terminals, and bots. You’ll run the conversations where a trading team decides which chain to build on.

  • Build and own a pipeline of top trading startups from first contact through launch on the Monad network, working closely with the VCs and accelerators funding them.

  • Own onboarding, launch, and post-launch success: coordinate technical onboarding with core contributors, scope liquidity and ecosystem incentive programs, run launch logistics, and track volume and retention after go-live.

  • Be a public voice for trading on the Monad network. Shape the narrative through content, interviews, podcasts, and speaking slots.

  • Bring market intelligence back in: what traders want, where competing chains are winning, which sub verticals are getting funded. Turn it into input for ecosystem priorities.

  • Build commercial proposals grounded in numbers: cost per retained user, volume sustained after incentives taper, and impact on network activity.

  • Make trading a priority across Monad Foundation’s work: marketing, events, and ecosystem programs.

Who You Are

  • Trading-native. You’re an active trader, or you’ve held a non-quant role (BD, product, growth) at a trading protocol. A generalist BD background alone doesn’t meet the bar.

  • Deeply networked among traders and trading teams, the people who actually choose where to build and trade.

  • Fluent in onchain trading mechanics: AMMs, orderbooks, execution quality, MEV, and liquidity incentives.

  • Comfortable with numbers. You can model whether an incentive program retains volume after it ends, explain a trading team’s revenue drivers, and hold your own with engineers and quants.

  • A strong communicator on paper, on stage, and in 1:1 conversations with founders.

  • High ownership, trustworthy, and you follow through.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Relationships with VCs and accelerators funding trading teams.

  • Access to specialized subnetworks: launchpads, perps, prediction markets, memecoin trading.

  • Relationships with market makers (a bonus; this area is already well covered).

Why Work with Us

  • Challenging problems. You’ll tackle deeply complex and technically demanding problems, with autonomy and impact.

  • Endless Opportunity for Impact. The Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) standard is ubiquitous, but existing EVM-compatible chains are slow and bandwidth-constrained. Monad’s core innovations offer developers and founders the best of both worlds (portability and performance) and are a game-changer to power global on-chain finance.

  • The right team. You’ll be part of a world class team, who are exceptional and highly-motivated.

  • Culture. We’re a lean team working together to achieve very ambitious goals. We are united in our culture of collaboration, low ego, and high-quality output.

  • Strong Ecosystem. The broader Monad ecosystem has attracted support from leading investors, builders and long-term contributors.

About the job

The Strategic Sourcing Analyst is a role responsible for driving end-to-end sourcing events, commercial negotiations, and contract structuring across key technology spend categories, including IT infrastructure, software, IT services, and staffing agencies. In this role, you will act as a trusted advisor to internal stakeholders, owning the entire sourcing lifecycle from initial market analysis and RFP execution to final contract drafting and vendor onboarding, ensuring optimal value and mitigated risk for the business.

“Negotiates high-value tech contracts and ensures we only pay for delivered results”

Responsibilities

  • Lead single-source negotiations and competitive RFPs across multiple technology and services spend categories.

  • Negotiate and secure favorable tier discounts, pricing models, and commercial terms with key technology and service vendors.

  • Structure complex Statements of Work (SOWs), ensuring that agency fee disbursements are strictly tied to measurable delivery milestones and performance metrics.

  • Standardize contractor rate cards and implement labor caps across all staff augmentation and external consulting engagements.

  • Conduct comprehensive market analysis to inform sourcing strategies and benchmark pricing.

  • Draft, review, and refine contract terms in close collaboration with Legal, Security, and Finance teams.

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with internal stakeholders, aligning sourcing strategies with broader organizational goals.

  • 5+ years of proven experience in strategic sourcing, procurement, or vendor management, with specific expertise in technology categories (Cloud, SaaS, IT Services, Staffing). 

  • Exceptional negotiation skills with a history of driving cost savings and favorable commercial terms. 

  • Deep understanding of contract structures, particularly in milestone-based SOWs and standardized labor rate cards. 

  • Strong analytical skills to evaluate market trends, pricing models, and total cost of ownership. 

  • Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to influence cross-functional teams in a fast-paced, remote-first environment.

  • Comfortable managing end-to-end sourcing processes without relying on heavy, legacy ERP systems.

Important information for candidates
Recruitment scams have become increasingly common. To protect yourself, please keep the following in mind when applying for roles:

  • Apply only through our official channels. We do not use third-party platforms or agencies for recruitment unless clearly stated. All open roles are listed on our official careers page: https://tether.recruitee.com/

  • Verify the recruiter’s identity. All our recruiters have verified LinkedIn profiles. If you’re unsure, you can confirm their identity by checking their profile or contacting us through our website.

  • Be cautious of unusual communication methods. We do not conduct interviews over WhatsApp, Telegram, or SMS. All communication is done through official company emails and platforms.

  • Double-check email addresses. All communication from us will come from emails ending in @tether.to or @tether.io

  • We will never request payment or financial details. If someone asks for personal financial information or payment at any point during the hiring process, it is a scam. Please report it immediately.

When in doubt, feel free to reach out through our official website.

Polymarket US operates under CFTC oversight as a regulated prediction market, which means the compliance function carries real regulatory weight. The AML team is responsible for detecting and reporting suspicious activity across a user base that transacts through card, ACH and stablecoin rails, and the work requires both financial crime expertise and the ability to think clearly about a product that looks different from a traditional bank or broker. The team is small and the caseload is real.

This hire matters because investigation quality is the core of what we do. You will own your casework, from initial review through SAR filing or documented declination, and your judgment will directly shape how the program holds up to regulatory scrutiny. You will also be a resource for the analysts around you, which means your standards become their standards.

The environment moves fast. Polymarket is growing, the regulatory landscape for prediction markets is still developing, and the compliance program is being built to match that pace. If you want a role where the work is clearly defined and the edge cases are rare, this is not it. If you want to do serious investigative work at a company where compliance has a seat at the table, it is.

What You'll Do

  • Investigate escalated cases from transaction monitoring, fraud referrals, market surveillance and sanctions screening for signs of money laundering, terrorist financing, fraud and sanctions evasion.

  • Prepare detailed Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) that meet regulatory requirements and internal policy, and document decisions when no SAR is needed.

  • Review customer identity and profile information to assess whether activity fits the customer's known background and stated purpose.

  • Support law enforcement requests, subpoenas and 314(a) reviews.

  • Demonstrated ability to analyze transaction activity across multiple payment rails and draw well-supported conclusions about the nature of that activity.

  • Clear written communication, specifically the ability to write SAR narratives that are accurate, organized and defensible.

  • Experience with investigative research tools such as CLEAR or LexisNexis, and with case management systems.

  • A track record of managing a caseload independently, meeting deadlines and maintaining quality under volume.

About Kamino

Kamino's mission is to create liquidity and utility for every asset. We want the world's best investments to be available through the financial platforms people already trust, and we want investors to be able to borrow against what they own when they need liquidity, instead of having to sell.

Today, the most valuable assets in the world are often the least useful to own. Trillions of dollars sit in private markets, behind high minimums and holding periods that can run for years. Tokenization is starting to move these assets onto shared, programmable infrastructure, but putting an asset onchain is only the first step. To be useful, it still needs distribution, compliance, servicing, credit and liquidity.

Kamino already runs the credit and liquidity engine at scale. It is the largest credit protocol on Solana and the largest credit platform for real-world assets onchain, with more than $650 billion in cumulative transaction volume and more than $20 billion in loans originated.

Now we are building the rest of that system for institutions. Kamino recently named Yieldstreet co-founder Michael Weisz as CEO and is building a new HQ in New York, alongside the asset managers and financial platforms that will shape this market. Almost none of that market exists yet, and we intend to build it.

Legal & Compliance | New York, NY | Full-time | Four days in office | Reports to the CEO

The opportunity

Kamino is hiring its first General Counsel to lead legal and compliance globally, build the U.S. operating foundation, and hire the legal and compliance team over the next 6–12 months.

Kamino is expanding in the United States and building a team in New York to lead this next phase. We are looking for a General Counsel who will own Kamino's global legal and compliance function and turn that ambition into an executable operating model.

As General Counsel, you will be accountable for legal and compliance matters across the globe. Your immediate focus will be establishing Kamino's U.S. operating foundation, while setting the global legal strategy and overseeing regulatory matters outside the U.S.

This is a build-with-product role, not a pure sign-off function. Working directly with the CEO and leaders across product, engineering, business development and operations, you will shape institutional products and partnerships from inception and turn regulatory sophistication into a commercial advantage. Within your first 6–12 months, you will begin building the legal and compliance team that will scale with Kamino.

What you'll do

Global legal and compliance leadership

  • Serve as Kamino's chief legal officer and principal legal adviser to the CEO, leadership team and the Foundation.

  • Own the global legal and compliance function across all Kamino entities and jurisdictions, including corporate, commercial, regulatory, intellectual property, employment, privacy and disputes.

  • Set Kamino's global regulatory strategy, coordinating U.S. work with frameworks such as MiCA and with other key markets.

  • Establish and oversee Kamino's global compliance program, including AML, sanctions, risk assessment, policies and monitoring.

  • Manage legal risk, disputes and any regulatory inquiries or investigations worldwide.

  • Own the legal and compliance budget, and select and manage external counsel and regulatory advisers across jurisdictions.

Building the legal and compliance team

  • Design the target structure of Kamino's legal and compliance organization, aligned to the company's product, geographic and institutional roadmap.

  • Begin hiring within the first 6–12 months, prioritizing the roles Kamino needs most (for example, compliance, product and regulatory counsel, and commercial counsel).

  • Recruit, develop and lead a high-performing team, and set the standards, tools and ways of working the function operates by.

  • Decide what to build in-house and what to keep with external counsel as Kamino scales.

U.S. legal architecture and governance

  • Design Kamino's U.S. legal and regulatory operating model, including entity roles, legal posture and the approval process for new products.

  • Partner with executive leadership to develop and refine the U.S. roadmap in line with Kamino's overall strategy, with legal and regulatory considerations built into planning from the outset.

  • Advise where Kamino should operate as infrastructure, where third parties must assume regulated or managerial responsibilities, and what Kamino should deliberately avoid.

Product roadmap and institutional strategy

  • Embed with product and engineering on lending markets, vaults, leverage products, points and rewards programs, token launches, tokenized real-world assets and other new capabilities.

  • Translate regulatory risk into concrete product design choices before products are built, rather than layering legal review on after decisions have been made.

  • Create repeatable legal and diligence processes for onboarding asset managers, curators, distribution platforms and supporting service providers.

  • Lead or support negotiations involving integrations, institutional pilots, data, technology, custody, servicing, tokenization, credit and liquidity.

Securities, commodities and regulatory analysis

  • Apply the Howey and Reves tests, related case law and CFTC jurisdictional principles to evaluate whether tokens, yield products or trading features could be characterized as securities or commodity derivatives under U.S. law.

  • Track and interpret federal legislation, SEC and CFTC rulemaking and guidance, state frameworks, and executive or agency policy affecting DeFi, staking, stablecoins, custody and tokenized assets, alongside major developments in other jurisdictions.

  • Assess money-transmitter licensing, BitLicense-style regimes and other state-level requirements for Kamino's operating entities, and equivalent licensing requirements in other markets.

Regulatory engagement, compliance and policy

  • Represent Kamino in proactive and responsive interactions with the SEC, CFTC, FinCEN, OFAC, relevant state regulators and, where relevant, non-U.S. regulators.

  • Advise on Bank Secrecy Act obligations, FinCEN guidance, OFAC sanctions screening and Travel Rule implications for non-custodial infrastructure and any centralized touchpoints.

  • Contribute to industry advocacy and help shape Kamino's comments on proposed rules through appropriate trade associations and policy organizations.

  • Build regulatory literacy across product, engineering and go-to-market teams so that sound judgment is applied without legal reviewing every routine decision.

  • Maintain legal memoranda, risk assessments, policies and decision logs for product launches.

What success looks like

Building the global legal and compliance foundation

Within the first six months

  • Make Kamino operational in the United States for its approved initial scope within 90 days, including the ability to employ its team, maintain its New York presence, enter contracts and advance approved business development and pilot activity.

  • Establish clear boundaries, decision rights and escalation processes.

  • Complete the licensing and registration analysis for Kamino's planned U.S. activities and establish the roadmap for any required approvals.

  • Map Kamino's legal and compliance obligations in its other key jurisdictions and put oversight and external counsel coverage in place.

  • Put the initial compliance, contracting, governance and documentation framework in place.

  • Produce executable legal pathways for Kamino's highest-priority institutional pilots and partnerships.

  • Agree a legal and compliance team plan and hiring priorities with the CEO, and begin recruiting for the first roles.

By the end of the first year

  • Make the first legal and compliance hires and have the core team operating.

  • Expand the initial U.S. structure into a scalable operating model capable of supporting institutional products and partnerships.

  • Establish repeatable legal processes for asset-manager onboarding, distribution integrations and institutional product launches.

  • Enable Kamino's priority institutional pilots to proceed with clear approvals, responsibilities and risk boundaries.

  • Implement practical global governance and compliance systems that protect Kamino without slowing product development.

  • Build a trusted network of external counsel, regulatory advisers and industry relationships across Kamino's key jurisdictions.

  • Set the longer-term roadmap for Kamino's global legal and compliance organization.

Why this role matters

The infrastructure decisions being made today will shape how institutions participate in onchain markets for years. Kamino has already built a proven credit and liquidity engine. The next challenge is to create the legal and operating framework, starting in the U.S., that allows that technology to serve asset managers, distribution platforms and financial institutions at scale.

As Kamino's first General Counsel, you will sit at the intersection of law, product and company building. You will help determine what Kamino builds, how it operates and which institutional opportunities it can pursue, and you will build the team that carries that work forward.

Who we are looking for

A practical legal builder and leader

Required

  • J.D. and active bar membership in at least one U.S. jurisdiction.

  • Twelve or more years of relevant legal and regulatory experience, including meaningful time in-house at a digital-asset or fintech company, in a law-firm digital-assets practice, or at a relevant regulator.

  • Experience leading a legal or compliance function, or a significant part of one, as the senior legal adviser to executive leadership.

  • A track record of hiring, managing and developing lawyers and compliance professionals.

  • Direct, hands-on experience with DeFi protocols and digital-asset market structure, including lending markets, automated market makers, liquidity vaults, staking and onchain governance.

  • Demonstrated experience interacting with the SEC, CFTC or other financial regulators through inquiries, comment letters, roundtables, no-action processes or enforcement matters.

  • Strong working knowledge of U.S. securities and commodities laws, the Bank Secrecy Act, sanctions requirements and relevant state regulatory frameworks as applied to digital assets.

  • Working knowledge of cross-border digital-asset regulatory frameworks, including MiCA and the U.K. FCA regime, and experience managing legal matters across multiple jurisdictions.

  • Fluency in the current U.S. legislative and regulatory landscape, with the ability to convert fast-moving developments into practical guidance.

  • Sound judgment and comfort operating where the law is still developing, with the confidence to recommend a course of action rather than simply identify risk.

  • Excellent communication with engineers, product leaders, commercial teams and boards in a way that supports product velocity.

  • Thoughtful use of modern technology, including AI, to improve legal research, drafting, regulatory tracking and execution.

Strongly preferred

  • Prior experience as General Counsel, Deputy General Counsel or Chief Compliance Officer at a digital-asset or fintech company.

  • Existing relationships within digital-asset policy, regulatory and institutional legal circles, in the U.S. and internationally.

  • Experience building an early-stage legal or compliance function from the ground up, including policies, licensing roadmaps and monitoring infrastructure.

  • Experience with Foundation, DAO or protocol governance structures and token-related legal matters.

  • Experience structuring institutional financial products, asset-manager relationships, distribution arrangements or tokenized real-world assets.

How we will work

  • Direct access to the CEO and close partnership with product, engineering, business development and operations.

  • Early involvement in strategy and product design, with visible decisions and fast escalation when an issue blocks progress.

  • High ownership, documented judgment, clear deadlines and a bias toward practical solutions.

  • Clear authority to shape and hire the legal and compliance team.

Compensation and benefits

Kamino expects to offer a competitive package consisting of base salary, a performance-based bonus and long-term KMNO participation.

Final terms will reflect the candidate's experience, scope and agreed role.

Kamino is building its U.S. benefits infrastructure. Health-coverage arrangements, paid time off, holidays, equipment, travel and expense policies will be documented as part of the formal offer.

Forward Deployed Product Manager

Location: U.S. (Remote, but must be based in the United States)

Travel: Depending on the assigned engagement, substantial travel to state government partner sites may be expected

Clearance: Must be eligible and able to pass a government background check

ABOUT SPRUCE

Our mission is to let users control their data across the web. We build privacy-preserving, standards-based digital identity and credentialing systems that help governments and institutions increase access to important services and benefits programs while reducing fraud. We believe the right approach to product management is critical to combining high standards of usability, security, and privacy into a seamless user experience and driving broad adoption.

THE ROLE

We are seeking a Forward Deployed Product Manager to sit alongside our government customers during discovery, architecture, and design, sometimes while engineering is building, and help them work out what they actually need and why.

You will support specific deployments, from statewide identity programs to large-scale education and workforce credentialing initiatives. Each must be localized to its own ecosystem: stakeholders, user demographics, regulations, and program objectives. Even as we sell a product to a customer, we treat the overall program as a product with its own governance, roadmap, and objectives. Much of this work is customer-driven today and requires hands-on engagement with individual implementations, even as we work to consolidate what we learn into reusable Spruce products. Holding both at once is the job.

A credential is only useful if someone issues it, someone accepts it, and someone carries it. So beyond discovery, you own adoption for your program: getting issuers to issue, verifiers to verify, and end users to adopt, with startup-style resourcefulness and measurable KPIs. In some cases, you will source and build the first pilot group yourself.

The surface area is broad, and you should be good at taming unknowns and complexity. One week you may be shaping the roadmap for a statewide digital identity wallet, the next a citizen-facing portal, the next the APIs and microservices underneath. You are responsible for the end-to-end product picture, how those pieces fit together, and ultimately outcomes for our customers’ customers.

This is not a roadmap-and-quarterly-planning role. We move quickly, put work in front of small pilot groups, and let evidence change the plan. At the same time, this is identity infrastructure, where security, accessibility, and reliability matter. Knowing what can be iterated on quickly and what absolutely cannot is central to doing this job well.

CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

1. CUSTOMER-EMBEDDED DISCOVERY

  • Work directly with state government partners through discovery, architecture, and design

  • Understand their users, policy environment, constraints, and workflows first-hand

  • Look past stated requirements to the underlying problem the customer is actually trying to solve

  • Navigate government relationships thoughtfully: introduce user evidence that may challenge stated priorities, and influence direction without damaging the relationship

2. END-TO-END PRODUCT OWNERSHIP

  • Hold the full product picture across user-facing experiences and the APIs and services beneath them, often across several interconnected initiatives at once

  • Help partners shape and sequence their roadmap, and make sure what gets built solves the real problem

  • Partner closely with engineering, design, and delivery leads from definition through deployment

3. HANDS-ON USER RESEARCH

  • Personally design and run research: talk to stakeholders and end users directly, run discovery, prototype where appropriate

  • Synthesize what you learn into product decisions and roadmap direction

  • Bring user evidence into conversations where requirements are often treated as fixed

There is no research team or technical product manager counterpart behind this role. You do this work yourself, whether that means digging into agency rules, legislation, user interviews, or codebases.

4. ECOSYSTEM BUILDING AND ADOPTION

  • Drive adoption of digital credentials across your program’s ecosystem: onboard issuers, verifiers, and institutional partners with startup GTM resourcefulness

  • Find high-leverage partnerships (university research programs, workforce boards, employer networks) that multiply impact beyond your own direct effort

  • Own adoption KPIs and find creative, resourceful ways to move them

5. JUDGMENT ABOUT PACE VERSUS RISK

  • Put work in front of small pilot groups early and let findings redirect the roadmap

  • Draw clear lines around what cannot be iterated on loosely: security, accessibility, and reliability

  • Make and defend those calls with engineering and with customers

Where this role ends. This is a forward-deployed role, not a core product role: you own outcomes for your engagements, not Spruce’s product-line roadmap. But you are the person closest to the field, so we expect you to notice when a problem extends beyond a single agency and flag what should become reusable Spruce capability.

WHAT YOU BRING

  • 6–10+ years of product experience at startups or on new product initiatives. Former founder or founding-team operator is the ideal profile

  • Zero-to-one experience: you have taken a product from nothing to shipped, or identified and pursued entirely new opportunities

  • Meaningful experience in education, workforce development, or adjacent sectors

  • A real interest in workforce development and expanding opportunity through technology

  • Experience in government or another highly regulated environment

Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

As a Global Investigator on the triage team, you are the first line of operational response in a fast-moving crypto disruption pipeline. You process inbound victim complaints, validate the output of our AI investigation tooling, and route cases into the investigative workflows that lead to frozen scam proceeds, takedowns, and recovered assets. You hold the disposition pen: your call is what turns a complaint into a freeze, an escalation, a recovery handoff, a victim notification, or a close.

The impact you will have:

  • Validate and route hundreds of complaint dispositions each week, feeding a live asset-recovery pipeline that gets stolen funds frozen before they move.

  • Use AI first-pass output as a co-pilot and catch the errors that matter, such as false positives, merged syndicates, and misclassified scam patterns, before they propagate downstream.

  • Enrich complaint selectors with a broad stack of commercial data-source integrations and on-chain and off-chain checks to decide what is actionable.

  • Own clean shift handoffs so the around-the-clock operation never drops a lead, keeping the US-hours queue moving for the rest of the triage team.

  • Feed structured signal back to engineering on where the AI triage model misses, so it gets more precise every week.

What we’re looking for:

  • Investigative or analytical experience in the private or public sector. 1-3 years is fine; we want people who want to grow into deep crypto expertise.

  • Strong AI fluency, meaning comfort using AI tools as a daily co-pilot to work a high-volume queue, with the judgment to know when the output is wrong.

  • Baseline crypto knowledge and the ability to recognize threat types such as investment scams, pig-butchering, and ransomware, and comfort pairing that with AI-assisted analysis.

  • Able to prioritize and work independently, with clear written handoffs, during hours when the rest of the team is offline.

  • Receptive to feedback from experienced tracers and engineers, and motivated to improve the triage process rather than only clear tickets.

  • US Citizenship required

  • Ability to obtain Public Trust clearance

About the Team:

  • The team pairs seasoned crypto tracers with rising investigators. Triage investigators sit alongside experienced Global Investigators and intelligence-trained individual contributors, and the seat is built to accelerate your development toward deeper tracing work.

  • The work is operationally hard: high volume, real victims, and time-sensitive calls where a fast, accurate disposition can be the difference between funds frozen and funds gone.

Team Operating Rhythms:

  • Primary coverage during US business hours in your local time zone, holding triage throughput while colleagues in other regions are offline.

  • Distributed, not distant: async-first handoffs, clear written updates, and tight coordination with global teammates on time-sensitive items.

Required online and collaboration hours:

  • Schedule: Standard North American EST business hours preferred, with overlap for daily handover to and from other regions.

On-Call Responsibilities:

  • Schedule: Formal on-call rotation for high-priority events, such as active hacks, law-enforcement support, and other time-sensitive matters.

  • Frequency: Weekly rotation, with occasional weekend coverage; remote standby (free to go about your day and respond when paged), not worksite-bound.

Travel Requirements:

  • Schedule: Minimal; occasional team or mission offsites.

Onsite Requirements:

  • Distributed/remote role with no routine onsite requirement.

Learn about TRM Speed in this position:

  • Within your first 30 days, you are clearing live complaint surges end to end, turning raw victim reports into actionable freezes and escalations the same day they arrive.

  • Within 90 days, your prioritization calls are routinely accepted by Global Investigators, measurably shortening the time between a report landing and funds being frozen.

  • Each week, your feedback to engineering sharpens the AI triage model, so the whole team catches more recoverable cases with less manual review.

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

  • Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

  • Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly

  • Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.
